answer:
At 700 bar and 25 °C (298.15 K), hydrogen has a density of about 39.2 kg/m³ (0.0392 g/cm³). I computed this with CoolProp, which uses the Leachman et al. (2009) equation of state for hydrogen.

- **Normal hydrogen:** 39.22 kg/m³.
- **Para-hydrogen:** 39.22 kg/m³ as well. At room temperature the spin form makes almost no difference.
- **Compressibility factor:** Z = 1.45. An ideal-gas estimate would give 56.9 kg/m³, which is about 45% too high, so a real-gas equation of state is needed at this pressure.

This agrees with the figure of about 39–40 kg/m³ commonly quoted for 700-bar fuel-cell vehicle tanks, though I am going by recall for that and did not check it against a second source.

No project files were created or changed.
